results.text: Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

Uplink loss of the base station, pairing timeouts, capacity limit reached, weak signal of a single device, low battery, outdated peripheral firmware that upgrades successfully via OTA, and full storage. Provide the customer with step-by-step instructions and confirm the issue is resolved.

complaint: Since last week we don't get any push notifications on our phones, even though the siren works when the alarm goes off at home. I reinstalled the app on both phones and it didn't help. Maybe the latest app version is just buggy? Is there an older version I can install?
usability_reason: The reply is clear and polite and gives a plausible root cause, but it is not actionable for the customer and makes unsupported claims: it asserts the base station has a cloud TLS problem, cites E-503/logs and a historical case, and says the case was escalated—none of which appear in the session record (no questions asked, no actions performed). It also does not address the customer's question about an older app version. It avoids claiming a fix was completed, which is positive, but the unsupported diagnostic and escalation claims limit the score.
